newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.N. official criticises deportations of Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official criticises deportations of Bosnians.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency criticised Germany on Sunday for forcing war refugees home to Bosnia, saying too many deportations would have a destabilising effect on the region.

Judith Kumin, the U.N. High Commission's representative in Germany, said refugees who came to Germany from parts of Bosnia now under the control of other ethnic groups should not be forced to return to homes that no longer exist.

"There is a risk of new tensions and social conflict if a large number of refugees are forced to live for a second time as refugees somewhere in Bosnia in a place that is not their home," Kumin said in an interview with the Tagesspiegel newspaper.
"It is our view that these people who cannot return to their home regions should not be forced to return," she said. "The return should contribute something positive to the entire peace process."
She said Germany was overlooking the question of how to ensure there was no new conflict in Bosnia.
Ignoring criticism from outside and inside the country, several cashed-strapped German states have begun forcibly repatriating some of the 320,000 Bosnians who sought refuge there during the war.
The states, which have been paying billions of marks (dollars) each year to support the refugees, had hoped they would voluntarily return after the fighting ended in late 1995.

The southern state of Bavaria has deported a total of 93 war refugees in recent months and 20 last week. The eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt last week sent home 30 Bosnia children and war orphans rescued from Sarajevo five years ago.
Berlin's interior minister Joerg Schoenbohm said on Sunday it was time that the the 36,000 Bosnian refugees there returned home.
"But the people who survived the civil war have suffered from different pressures and challenges as those who escaped the war here as refugees," he told ZDF television.
"I believe it is now time that they work together with their countrymen to rebuild their nation and not leave it all to those who suffered through the war."
Several leading German public figures, including former foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher, recently made a public appeal for changes to the practice of forcibly repatriating Bosnian refugees.

The signatories of the appeal, addressed to Interior Minister Manfred Kanther and his regional state counterparts, said the current practice could lead to increased tension in Bosnia and was damaging Germany's international image.
They singled out the deportation earlier this week of a group of Bosnian refugees from Berlin and Bavaria for criticism.
"Among those deported were pregnant women, patients receiving treatment for heart illness and other people whose deportation is incomprehensibe," the signatories said.
Kanther and state interior ministers agreed last year the refugees could be forcibly reptatriated if they refused to go.
